## Load packages

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)

# Including my traditional diagnostics package...  See the following for details:
# https://statacumen.com/teach/ADA1/help/Erhardt_R_Install.html
# The usual function call here is e_plot_lm_diagnostics(df, sw_plot_set = "simple")
if ((requireNamespace("erikmisc", quietly = TRUE)) == FALSE) {
  remotes::install_github("erikerhardt/erikmisc")
}
library(erikmisc)

set.seed(6979)
```

## Load the Data

```{r}
ed_data <- read.csv("final_data.csv")
#Remove entries without median debt reported, and turn it into a numeric.
ed_data <- ed_data |> subset(DEBT_MDN != "PS")
ed_data$DEBT_MDN <- as.numeric(ed_data$DEBT_MDN)
# Clean up all factors which were imported as integers.
ed_data$CONTROL.x <- as.factor(ed_data$CONTROL.x)
ed_data$REGION <- as.factor(ed_data$REGION)
ed_data$HIGHDEG <-as.factor(ed_data$HIGHDEG)
ed_data$PREDDEG <- as.factor(ed_data$PREDDEG)
ed_data$NUMBRANCH <- as.factor(ed_data$NUMBRANCH)
ed_data$MAIN.x <-as.factor(ed_data$MAIN.x)
ed_data$SCH_DEG <- as.factor(ed_data$SCH_DEG)
#Now lets turn all of our numeric data that got converted into character back into numeric data, changing NA values to zero for simplicity
cols_to_convert <- c("DEBT_MDN", "DEATH_YR8_RT", "COMP_ORIG_YR8_RT", "COMP_4YR_TRANS_YR8_RT", "PELL_COMP_4YR_TRANS_YR8_RT", "PELL_WDRAW_ORIG_YR8_RT", "NOPELL_WDRAW_ORIG_YR8_RT", "NOT1STGEN_COMP_4YR_TRANS_YR2_RT","FIRSTGEN_COMP_ORIG_YR2_RT", "DEBT_MDN","CREDDESC","DEBT_ALL_STGP_ANY_MEAN","BBRR1_FED_UG_DFLT"  )

new_ed_data <- ed_data %>%
  mutate(across(
    all_of(cols_to_convert),
    ~ {
      x <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.x))
      replace(x, is.na(x), 0)
    }
  ))

# Let's center our data first...  Fix this shit later.  It isn't doing anything right now.
centered_ed_data <- ed_data
numeric_cols <- sapply(df, is.numeric)
centered_ed_data[numeric_cols] <- lapply(centered_ed_data[numeric_cols], scale, scale = FALSE)
rm(numeric_cols)

#model_1 <- lm(EARN_MDN_4YR ~ , data = centered_ed_data)
#model_2 <- lm(EARN_MDN_4YR ~ , data = centered_ed_data)
model_3 <- lm(EARN_MDN_4YR ~ (TUITIONFEE_IN + CONTROL.x + ADM_RATE_ALL)^2 + PREDDEG + HIGHDEG + C150_4 + DEBT_MDN, data = centered_ed_data)
```

## 1. Multiple regression models (10 pts)

At least two candidate models with several predictors are fit. Coefficients are interpreted correctly, holding the other predictors fixed. Categorical predictors are coded and interpreted correctly.

## 2. Interactions and polynomial terms (10 pts)

At least one interaction or polynomial term is considered, with a reason for it. It is tested (for example, a partial F test or a test) and the result is stated. An interaction plot or fitted-curve plot is included where relevant. A well-reasoned term that turns out not to help still earns full credit.

## 3. Diagnostics (10 pts)

Residual plots and checks for the model’s assumptions are shown. Outliers, influential points, or multicollinearity (VIF) are examined. The report says what the checks found, even if nothing was wrong.

## 4. Model selection and justification (10 pts)

Candidate models are compared with a stated criterion (adjusted $R^2$, AIC, BIC, $C_p$, or an F test). The final model is chosen and the choice is justified in words. NoteSTAT 540 groups: deeper selection justification In addition to the above, a 540 group compares at least three candidate models using at least two different criteria. Where the criteria disagree, the report explains why and says what the group traded off (fit against parsimony, or prediction against interpretation). Award 10 only if this is done. This is part of the criterion, not extra points.

## 5. Integration and reproducibility (10 pts) - COMPLETE

The report builds on Milestone 2 and responds to its feedback. The submission is a rendered PDF named Group_XX_Milestone3.pdf, with code visible, a seed set, and sessionInfo() present.
